retrieved.title: TRL 2 — Technology concept formulated
retrieved.content: Once basic principles are observed, practical applications can be speculated upon, but they remain analytic; no experimental proof or detailed analysis yet supports the invention. For a startup, this looks like a named product concept and an architecture sketch describing how the underlying principle would solve a specific problem, backed by rough back-of-envelope reasoning rather than any built code or lab result.
retrieved.citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

retrieved.title: TRL 3 — Experimental proof of concept
retrieved.content: Active research and development is initiated, including analytical and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology. For a startup, this means a scoped experiment or a proof-of-concept script has produced a recorded result showing the core mechanism functions in isolation, even though no components have been integrated into a working prototype.
retrieved.citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

retrieved.title: MRL 3 — Informal problem interviews
retrieved.content: The team has held informal conversations with prospective buyers — problem interviews or casual conversations at events — surfacing anecdotal interest, but no prospect has made any commitment. Evidence is a set of interview notes or call logs showing a handful of conversations, with reactions recorded but no willingness-to-pay signal.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: MRL 4 — Structured customer discovery
retrieved.content: Customer discovery has been formalized: structured interviews have been run across multiple prospects using a consistent script, and a common pain point has been validated across that sample. Evidence is a discovery report summarizing interview themes across a named number of prospects, though no prospect has yet indicated a specific willingness to pay.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: RRL 1 — No regulatory analysis
retrieved.content: No analysis has been done of which laws, regulations, or licensing regimes apply to the product or its operation; the regulatory landscape is entirely unknown to the team. Evidence at this level is the absence of any regulatory review — no memo, no advisor engaged, no list of candidate rules.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: RRL 2 — Regulatory domain identified
retrieved.content: The team has identified which regulatory domain and which oversight body plausibly governs the product — for example, data protection, financial services, or medical device rules — but has not obtained any formal legal assessment of what specifically applies. Evidence is an internal note naming the likely regulator or regulatory area, based on the team's own research rather than counsel.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ARL 3 — Informal demo reactions
retrieved.content: The product concept has been shown to a handful of prospective users through informal demos, and their verbal reactions have been captured, but no behavior has actually been measured — reactions are qualitative impressions only. Evidence is a log of demo sessions with recorded verbal feedback from a small number of people.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ARL 4 — Structured usability testing
retrieved.content: Structured usability or concept-testing sessions have been run with prospective users, collecting task-completion and satisfaction data, but every interaction has occurred under direct observation rather than independent use. Evidence is a usability test report with task-completion rates and satisfaction scores from a defined set of observed sessions.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ORL 2 — Informal division of responsibilities
retrieved.content: Founders have informally divided responsibilities between themselves based on skill or interest, but nothing is written down and decisions are still made ad hoc rather than through any agreed process. Evidence is, at most, an informal verbal understanding of who handles what, with no written role description or org chart.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ORL 3 — First non-founder contributor
retrieved.content: A first contributor beyond the founders — a contractor, advisor, or part-time hire — has joined the venture, but there is still no formal governance structure or documented operating process guiding how work happens. Evidence is a contract or engagement letter for the first non-founder contributor, with no accompanying process documentation.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: IRL 1 — No funding plan, founder time only
retrieved.content: No funding plan exists at all: the venture is running on founder time and personal resources with no target raise amount, no use-of-funds outline, and no investor contact of any kind. Evidence is simply the absence of any funding document or investor conversation.

retrieved.title: IRL 2 — Informal funding hypothesis
retrieved.content: An informal funding hypothesis has been noted — a general sense that a seed round will eventually be needed — but no target amount, use-of-funds outline, or investor list has been drafted. Evidence is, at most, a passing mention in founder notes rather than any funding document.

byDim.Technology: AgroLink PH formulated its mobile-first concept with SMS fallback and tested a paper prototype of the lot-aggregation flow with 3 cooperatives in September 2025. To advance, backend engineer Ana Beltran and the team must move beyond paper prototypes to build and run proof-of-concept scripts that experimentally validate core isolation mechanisms of the platform.
byDim.Market: The team conducted field interviews with 18 cooperatives in June 2025 and secured a provisional agreement with one institutional buyer in January 2026. To progress, the team must formalize customer discovery using structured scripts across target rice and vegetable cooperatives in Nueva Ecija and Tarlac to validate pain points and willingness-to-pay signals.
byDim.Acceptance: Initial qualitative reactions were gathered during paper prototype testing with 3 cooperatives in September 2025. To advance, AgroLink PH needs to conduct structured usability testing sessions with cooperative officers under direct observation, collecting quantitative task-completion rates and satisfaction metrics for the lot-aggregation interface.
byDim.Organizational: Founders Rafael Domingo and Ana Beltran committed full-time in January 2026. To advance organizational readiness, the venture needs to contract or hire its first non-founder contributor and document initial role definitions and operational processes, such as decision logs or onboarding guides.
byDim.Regulatory: AgroLink PH has filed no patents and has not registered its wordmark with IPOPHL. To advance regulatory readiness, the team needs to engage external legal counsel for a preliminary opinion on regulatory requirements and draft a documented checklist of required permits and certifications.
byDim.Investment: The startup has recorded no revenue to date. To build investment readiness, AgroLink PH must draft a formal funding plan outlining a target raise amount and use-of-funds breakdown, then initiate initial pitch meetings with prospective investors.

byDim.Technology: The platform features a mobile-first design concept with SMS fallback, and a paper prototype of the lot-aggregation flow was tested in 2025-09. Led by backend engineer Ana Beltran, no functional software is built yet. To advance, the team needs to build and validate an experimental proof-of-concept script for the core aggregation mechanism.
byDim.Market: Field interviews were conducted with 18 cooperatives in 2025-06, and a provisional agreement was reached with one buyer in 2026-01, targeting 400 cooperatives in Nueva Ecija and Tarlac. To progress, the team needs to formalize structured discovery reports across target cooperatives and establish validated willingness-to-pay signals.
byDim.Acceptance: A paper prototype of the lot-aggregation flow was tested with 3 cooperatives in 2025-09 to gather early feedback. To advance acceptance, AgroLink PH needs to run structured usability testing sessions with cooperative officers to measure task-completion rates and user satisfaction under direct observation.
byDim.Organizational: Founders Rafael Domingo (6 years extension officer) and Ana Beltran (4 years backend engineer) committed full-time in 2026-01. To advance organizational readiness, the startup needs to bring on its first non-founder contributor, draft formal role definitions, and document initial operating processes.
byDim.Regulatory: No patents have been filed, and the AgroLink PH wordmark is not registered with IPOPHL. To move forward, the startup must engage legal counsel to receive a preliminary opinion on compliance requirements and register its wordmark with IPOPHL.
byDim.Investment: The venture has recorded zero revenue to date. To advance investment readiness, AgroLink PH needs to create a written funding plan specifying target raise amounts and use of funds, prepare a pitch deck, and initiate preliminary investor discussions.

retrieved.title: TRL 6 — Technology demonstrated in relevant environment
retrieved.content: A representative model or prototype system, well beyond the level tested for TRL 5, is tested in a relevant environment, going beyond laboratory testing to simulated operational conditions. A startup at this level has run a pilot with a small number of real customers in their own environment, delivering an end-to-end result and capturing structured feedback, though the deployment is limited in scale and duration.
retrieved.citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

retrieved.title: TRL 7 — System prototype demonstration in operational environment
retrieved.content: A prototype implementation, near or at the scale of the planned operational system, is demonstrated in an actual operational environment. For a startup, this looks like a substantially complete version of the product running live for real customers under actual operating conditions, in a limited rollout rather than a full launch, with monitoring in place to capture how it behaves outside a controlled trial.
retrieved.citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

retrieved.title: MRL 5 — Paid pilots with named customers
retrieved.content: Demand has moved from stated interest to a financial commitment: the startup has run repeated paid pilots with named customers, each willing to pay for a defined trial period. Evidence is signed pilot agreements or purchase orders from more than one named customer, together with pilot usage or outcome data collected during the engagement.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: MRL 6 — Repeat sales beyond initial pilots
retrieved.content: The customer base has expanded beyond the original pilots — additional paying customers have been acquired using a pitch or process that is starting to repeat — but there is no scalable acquisition channel yet and each sale still depends heavily on founder involvement. Evidence is a growing list of paying customers with dates of acquisition, plus early renewal or expansion revenue from at least one pilot customer.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: RRL 1 — No regulatory analysis
retrieved.content: No analysis has been done of which laws, regulations, or licensing regimes apply to the product or its operation; the regulatory landscape is entirely unknown to the team. Evidence at this level is the absence of any regulatory review — no memo, no advisor engaged, no list of candidate rules.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: RRL 2 — Regulatory domain identified
retrieved.content: The team has identified which regulatory domain and which oversight body plausibly governs the product — for example, data protection, financial services, or medical device rules — but has not obtained any formal legal assessment of what specifically applies. Evidence is an internal note naming the likely regulator or regulatory area, based on the team's own research rather than counsel.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ARL 5 — Measured usage by trial users
retrieved.content: Real users beyond the founding team have used the product independently in a trial, and their usage has actually been measured rather than merely observed. Evidence is trial usage data — session logs, feature-usage counts, or completion events — captured from named non-founder users without the founders present.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ARL 6 — Repeat usage and first referrals
retrieved.content: The trial cohort has expanded and users are returning for repeat sessions rather than trying the product once, with engagement metrics such as return rate now tracked, and the first organic, unprompted referrals from users to their peers have begun to appear. Evidence is a return-rate metric across a named trial cohort plus at least one documented organic referral.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ORL 2 — Informal division of responsibilities
retrieved.content: Founders have informally divided responsibilities between themselves based on skill or interest, but nothing is written down and decisions are still made ad hoc rather than through any agreed process. Evidence is, at most, an informal verbal understanding of who handles what, with no written role description or org chart.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: ORL 3 — First non-founder contributor
retrieved.content: A first contributor beyond the founders — a contractor, advisor, or part-time hire — has joined the venture, but there is still no formal governance structure or documented operating process guiding how work happens. Evidence is a contract or engagement letter for the first non-founder contributor, with no accompanying process documentation.
retrieved.citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

retrieved.title: IRL 1 — No funding plan, founder time only
retrieved.content: No funding plan exists at all: the venture is running on founder time and personal resources with no target raise amount, no use-of-funds outline, and no investor contact of any kind. Evidence is simply the absence of any funding document or investor conversation.

retrieved.title: IRL 2 — Informal funding hypothesis
retrieved.content: An informal funding hypothesis has been noted — a general sense that a seed round will eventually be needed — but no target amount, use-of-funds outline, or investor list has been drafted. Evidence is, at most, a passing mention in founder notes rather than any funding document.

byDim.Technology: MediSync Cebu demonstrated its structured referral record platform in a relevant environment through a 2025-02 pilot with 2 rural health units and 1 district hospital, expanding to 6 facilities by 2025-08 (TRL 6). To reach TRL 7, the system must be demonstrated at full scale in live operational conditions across Cebu's 44 rural health units, 8 district hospitals, and 3 tertiary referral centres.
byDim.Market: MediSync Cebu secured paid facility subscriptions across 6 facilities in 2025-08 and achieved PHP 5,000 monthly recurring revenue by 2026-02 (MRL 5). To advance to MRL 6, the venture needs repeat sales beyond initial pilots, acquiring additional paying facilities across Cebu's 44 rural health units, 8 district hospitals, and 3 tertiary centres, alongside subscription renewals.
byDim.Acceptance: Trial users across pilot facilities use the system to transmit referral records, bed availability, triage categories, and clinical history (ARL 5). To advance to ARL 6, MediSync Cebu must measure return rates across a defined cohort of healthcare users and document organic, unprompted referrals from facility staff to peer institutions.
byDim.Organizational: The team has 3 founders—Dr. Elena Reyes, Marco Villanueva, and Joy Tabotabo—who informally divide responsibilities (ORL 2). To progress to ORL 3, MediSync Cebu must engage its first non-founder contributor, such as a contractor, advisor, or part-time hire, to support provincial deployment.
byDim.Regulatory: No regulatory analysis has been conducted regarding laws or licensing for transmitting patient clinical histories across health facilities (RRL 1). To reach RRL 2, the team must perform initial research to identify the applicable regulatory domains and governing bodies overseeing healthcare data and systems in the Philippines.
byDim.Investment: The venture operates solely on founder time and personal resources, generating PHP 5,000 MRR without a funding plan or investor outreach (IRL 1). To reach IRL 2, MediSync Cebu needs to formulate an informal funding hypothesis outlining target capital requirements and potential use of funds to support system expansion.

byDim.Market: Current Level: MRL 5. Converted initial pilot sites to paid facility subscriptions in Aug 2025, reaching PHP 5,000 MRR by Feb 2026. Needs: Advance to ARL 6 by tracking return rates, demonstrating repeat ongoing usage by healthcare workers, and documenting the first unprompted organic referrals.

byDim.Regulatory: Current Level: RRL 1. No regulatory analysis has been conducted for the platform (though a trademark application is pending with IPOPHL). Needs: Advance to RRL 2 by identifying the applicable regulatory domain and oversight bodies governing health data and referral systems.
byDim.Investment: Current Level: IRL 1. Currently operating solely on founder time and personal resources alongside PHP 5,000 MRR without a funding plan. Needs: Advance to IRL 2 by forming an informal funding hypothesis regarding future capital needs and potential target raise amounts.

byDim.Technology: Currently at TRL 6, MediSync Cebu demonstrated its system in pilots starting with 2 rural health units and 1 district hospital, expanding to 6 facilities. To reach TRL 7, the team needs to demonstrate a substantially complete system operating live across Cebu's target facilities (44 RHUs, 8 district hospitals, 3 tertiary centers), maintaining real-time bed availability and referral record transmission with full monitoring under operational conditions outside controlled trials.
byDim.Market: Currently at MRL 5, having secured paid facility subscriptions in August 2025 and PHP 5,000 monthly recurring revenue by February 2026. To advance to MRL 6, the startup needs to expand sales beyond initial pilots across Cebu's 44 rural health units, 8 district hospitals, and 3 tertiary referral centers, documenting acquisition dates and securing early renewal or subscription expansion revenue.
byDim.Acceptance: Currently at ARL 5, with measured usage captured from trial users in operating facilities. To reach ARL 6, MediSync Cebu must measure return rates and repeat session usage among healthcare staff transmitting referral records and checking bed status, while securing and documenting the first unprompted organic referral from active users to peer facilities.
byDim.Organizational: Currently at ORL 3, led by 3 founders (Dr. Elena Reyes, Marco Villanueva, Joy Tabotabo) alongside a first non-founder contributor. To achieve ORL 4, the startup must draft formal role definitions for the core team, create initial operational process artifacts like onboarding checklists or decision logs, and prepare for its first full-time hire beyond the founding team.
byDim.Regulatory: Currently at RRL 3, with legal counsel engaged and a trademark application pending with IPOPHL. To reach RRL 4, MediSync Cebu needs to document a detailed regulatory checklist specifying the exact permits, health data privacy standards, and local governance compliance standards required to handle clinical histories and digital referrals across public health facilities.
byDim.Investment: Currently at IRL 3, with a drafted funding plan and PHP 5,000 in monthly recurring revenue achieved by February 2026. To reach IRL 4, the startup must convert its funding plan into an investor pitch deck or one-pager, initiate warm-intro investor meetings, and maintain an active log of investor pitches conducted.

byDim.Technology: Current Status: TRL 6. The referral coordination system was piloted in 2025-02 with 2 RHUs and 1 district hospital, expanding to 6 facilities by 2025-08. Needs: Demonstrate the system running live under actual operating conditions across additional target facilities (out of 44 RHUs, 8 district hospitals, and 3 tertiary centers) with operational monitoring in place to reach TRL 7.
byDim.Market: Current Status: MRL 5. Reached PHP 5,000 monthly recurring revenue by 2026-02 from paid facility subscriptions initiated in 2025-08. Needs: Acquire additional paying clinic or hospital customers beyond the initial pilot cohort using a standardized process, securing early renewals or expansion revenue to achieve MRL 6.
byDim.Acceptance: Current Status: ARL 5. Measured usage by independent healthcare trial users has been established across deployed facilities. Needs: Track cohort return rates for recurring clinical usage and document the first unprompted, organic referrals from active health workers to peer facilities to reach ARL 6.
byDim.Organizational: Current Status: ORL 3. The team consists of 3 founders (Dr. Elena Reyes, Marco Villanueva, Joy Tabotabo). Needs: Draft formal role definitions, document basic team processes (such as onboarding guides or decision logs), and evaluate hiring the first full-time non-founder team member to reach ORL 4.
byDim.Regulatory: Current Status: RRL 3. IPOPHL trademark application is pending, with no patents filed. Needs: Assemble a documented requirements checklist detailing the specific permits, regulatory standards, and compliance certifications needed for health referral software to reach RRL 4.
byDim.Investment: Current Status: IRL 3. A basic funding plan exists alongside PHP 5,000 MRR. Needs: Complete a pitch deck or one-pager and conduct initial investor conversations, logging meetings held with targeted investors to reach IRL 4.
